sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: És (and) and de (but) join words or clauses much like their English equivalents. De always comes after the first clause, not at the very start of the sentence.

items.english: I would like soup and salad.

items.spanish: Éhes vagyok, de nem vagyok szomjas.
items.english: I'm hungry, but I'm not thirsty.

sections.content: Éhes vagyok, de nem vagyok szomjas: de sits between the two clauses, exactly where 'but' would go in English.
